migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Language Quality findings were independently re-adjudicated against the current fixed five-component design rubric. Legacy normalized scores were retained only for audit and were not used to derive component levels. The snapshot is bound to exact source evidence and the current validator recomputes scores.

recertifier.provider_model_provenance_claim: No Anthropic/Sonnet call is claimed for these reconstructed judgments.

component_findings.async_structured: Recertified level 2 under the current criterion: Asynchronous concurrency has first-class composition and structured lifetime/join/cancellation mechanisms or an equivalent disciplined model. Evidence basis: Current Quidra provides bounded structured task.all execution, ordered scalar result transfer, atomic.Counter shared state and explicit GPU asynchronous execution/synchronization; general cancellation, channels/actors and broad synchronization remain limited. Preserved paid evidence additionally records: No executable Quidra concurrency workload/program was available under the readable template paths to empirically exercise task.all/atomic.Counter; assessment is documentation-only. | The standard-namespace list explicitly reserves `task` and `atomic` as concurrency-related namespaces alongside `ref`, `gpu`, etc. | 'Implementation scope' explicitly states the native core supports 'bounded structured concurrency through task.all for capture-free effect-only operations, ordered int[] / float[] scalar results, and explicit atomic.Counter shared state.' | This documents a narrow, structured-concurrency-only model: task.all is a bounded fork-join primitive over capture-free (no closures capturing mutable outer state) effect-only tasks, producing ordered int[]/float[] aggregated results, plus one atomic counter type for shared mutable state. | 'Cancellation' is explicitly listed as a remaining development area, implying task.all currently lacks cancellation support. | No general-purpose thread spawning, channels/message-passing, async/await syntax, futures/promises, actor model, or general shared-mutable-state primitives (locks, mutexes, condition variables, general atomics beyond Counter) are documented anywhere in the spec. | The `&` reference/address model is carefully specified for sequential-code aliasing safety, but the spec does not describe how its flow-sensitive guarantees in…

metric.concurrency.limitations: Current Quidra judgments are valid only for the exact compiler/runtime plus docs/tests identities frozen in this snapshot; relevant target changes must miss.
metric.concurrency.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic concurrency/parallelism semantics and core runtime primitives. External frameworks and debugger/tool maturity are out of scope.

component_findings.abi_calling_control: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: Current Quidra documents explicit extern C declarations, FFI-specific diagnostics, a restricted ABI-safe scalar/string/bin/callback subset, reference restrictions and symbol-conflict checks; aggregate layout coverage and broader ABI/callback surface remain intentionally limited. Preserved paid evidence additionally records: No FFI example program was available under the readable template paths; assessment is documentation-only against the frozen language spec. | No 'extern', 'ffi', 'foreign', 'cdecl', 'dlopen', or C-ABI declaration syntax appears anywhere in the documented surface language. | The 'Implementation scope' section explicitly enumerates what the native core currently supports (fixed-width numerics, casts, bin, arrays, tensors, image I/O, console I/O, namespaces, generics, classes, function values, bounded structured concurrency via task.all, atomic.Counter) and does not list any FFI/foreign-function/native-library-binding capability. | That same section names remaining development areas explicitly ('Cancellation, broader managed result transfer, self-hosting, broader signal-processing APIs, and broader package distribution') without naming general native interoperability as present or planned. | 'bin' is a packed raw-bit-sequence value type with explicit conversions to/from integers, bools, and flat arrays -- a plausible building block for a future binary/ABI marshaling layer -- but no calling convention, symbol linkage, header/binding generation, or foreign memory-ownership model is specified. | GPU/tensor sections describe explicit internal integration with backend-native libraries (CUDA Driver API, HIP runtime, Metal), but this is compiler/runtime-internal device integration, not a…
